newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's KomiTEK says investment tender falls.
newsitem.headline: Russia's KomiTEK says investment tender falls.

text.p: Russian oil company NK KomiTEK said an investment tender for 38 percent of the company, scheduled for December 6, had not been completed because of administrative problems.
KomiTEK, jointly owned by the state and the far northern Komi regional government, said in a statement current regulations did not cover selling such jointly-owned property.

Komitek said a five-party agreement, including the State Property Committee, Federal Property Fund and local authorities, had been drawn up in an effort to fill the legal vacuum but had not been able to do so.
The company said it hoped that rules would be worked out soon to allow a new tender to take place.
Komitek's main production unit is AO Komineft.
It did not say how many bids had been made for the 63.14 million shares. The starting price was 22.10 billion roubles for the whole stake or 350 roubles a share.

The minimum investment was $14 million. The money was to be used to build a pipeline. However, if the winner offered more than the minimum investment, the surplus would be used to pay the company's debts to the government.

The Federal Bankruptcy Administration (FUDN) said last Wednesday that it had summoned officials of KomiTEK and Sidanko to discuss susbsidiaries' tax arrears and debts to the pension fund. A statement said KomiTEK subsidiaries owed 290 billion roubles.
